dedupe_keys.name: carma platform fhwa open source software for cooperative driving automation research on connected automated vehicles

description: CARMA is the Federal Highway Administration's open-source research platform for cooperative driving automation, in which connected automated vehicles coordinate with each other and with road infrastructure. It is developed by the FHWA Saxton Transportation Operations Laboratory with a community of engineers and researchers under agile, open-source practice. Coverage: generic software, tested on US research vehicles and test tracks. CARMA Platform controls SAE level 2 connected automated vehicles through navigation (localisation), guidance (trajectory planning with third-party plugins through a generic API) and vehicle control, and supports cooperative manoeuvres such as cooperative lane changes; the wider CARMA programme publishes further repositories for infrastructure-side and simulation integration. Format and access: C++ code running in the Robot Operating System (ROS, migrating from ROS 1 to ROS 2) on Ubuntu, with Docker images and releases on GitHub; free. Licence: Apache 2.0. Caveats: the platform is for research on properly equipped vehicles, not for production use, and needs vehicle-specific drivers and calibration. Simulation uses: testing cooperative automation and vehicle-to-infrastructure applications in digital twin and co-simulation set-ups, and producing traffic behaviour for capacity planning of automated corridors. Related records: CARLA (platform-carla) is a driving simulator that can host such vehicle software, and SUMO (platform-sumo) provides the surrounding traffic.
